newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:

* General Motors Corp agreed to sell its military business operations of Hughes Electronics Corp to Raytheon Co in a deal valued at $9.5 billion. Raytheon edged out Northrop Grumman Corp in the bidding for the defence contractor.
* America Online Inc said it will increase spending to expand its network to placate angry subscribers to the congested online service.
* UAL Corp, which is one of the largest employee owned companies in the United States, is undergoing some stress in its relationship with its unions.
* Morgan Stanley Group Inc has restructured into two main divisions -- one focusing on securities and the other on asset management.
* Eastman Kodak Co reported higher fourth quarter operating profits, sending its shares higher. Also, the company plans to cut 4,000 jobs in Europe.
* Digital Equipment Corp regained profitability in the second quarter after a loss in its fiscal first quarter.
* General Electric Co's fourth quarter profits surged to $2.07 billion.
* The Dow Jones Industrial Average increased 38.49 points to close at 6765.37, its seventh record in two weeks.
* Ford Motor Co is cutting 1,300 jobs in England.
* Daimler-Benz AG said Helmut Werner resigned as head of Mercedes Benz.
* Allen Questrom plans to resign as chairman and chief executive of Federated Department Stores Inc.
* Australia's F.A.I. Insurances Ltd is turning its St. Moritz Hotel into luxury condominiums under a development deal with Donald Trump.
* Living standards have increased dramatically for South Korean workers, but a new law is increasing anxiety about job security.
* Chicago replaced an aging air traffic control computer that was regarded as one of its weakest links in the U.S. air traffic control system.
